# Zoro.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/zoro-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/zoro-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product and search listing data from Zoro.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Zoro.com in 2026 (without getting blocked)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-zoro-dot-com)
- **Code:** [`zoro.py`](zoro.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Product](results/product.json) · [Search listing](results/search_listing.json)

## What it scrapes

- Zoro.com product pages for detailed product data, specifications, images, ratings, and reviews
- Zoro.com search listing pages for product listings with metadata

## Functions

- `scrape_product(urls)` → `List[ZoroProduct]`: Scrape Zoro product pages for product data
- `scrape_search_listing(query, max_pages=3, scrape_all_pages=False, sort_by=None, sort_order='asc', filters=None)` → `ZoroSearchListing`: Scrape Zoro search pages for product listings

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import zoro


async def main():
    search_listing = await zoro.scrape_search_listing("Gloves", filters={"sort": "desc|averageRating"})


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`ZoroReview`**: `review_id?`, `rating?`, `headline`, `comments`, `nickname`, `location`, `created_date`, `is_verified_buyer`, `helpful_votes`, `media_count`
- **`ZoroProduct`**: `sku`, `mpn`, `name`, `brand`, `description`, `price`, `currency`, `availability`, `url`, `specifications`, `images`, `rating?`, `review_count`, `reviews`
- **`ZoroSearchListing`**: `total_pages`, `total_results`, `products`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`zoro.py`](zoro.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/zoro-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
